subject: HTI
name: Haiti
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: Columbus lands on Hispaniola
claims.summary: Christopher Columbus reaches the Taino island of Quisqueya and names it La Isla Espanola, beginning Spanish colonisation of the Americas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1492-columbus-lands-on-hispaniola, claim TL:HTI:event:1492:columbus-lands-on-hispaniola, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Collapse of the Taino
claims.summary: Forced labour, violence, and Old World disease devastate the Indigenous population within a generation of contact.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1500-collapse-of-the-taino, claim TL:HTI:event:1500:collapse-of-the-taino, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France gains Saint-Domingue
claims.summary: The Treaty of Rijswijk transfers the western third of Hispaniola from Spain to France, creating the colony of Saint-Domingue.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1697-france-gains-saint-domingue, claim TL:HTI:event:1697:france-gains-saint-domingue, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: World's richest colony
claims.summary: Saint-Domingue, with roughly half a million enslaved Africans, has become the leading producer of sugar and coffee and France's most valuable colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1789-world-s-richest-colony, claim TL:HTI:event:1789:world-s-richest-colony, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The slave uprising begins
claims.summary: A massive revolt of the enslaved erupts on the northern plain of Saint-Domingue, opening the Haitian Revolution.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1791-the-slave-uprising-begins, claim TL:HTI:event:1791:the-slave-uprising-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Napoleon's expedition; Toussaint deported
claims.summary: Napoleon sends an army to restore slavery; Toussaint Louverture is seized and deported to France, where he dies in 1803.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1802-napoleon-s-expedition-toussaint-deported, claim TL:HTI:event:1802:napoleon-s-expedition-toussaint-deported, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence proclaimed
claims.summary: Jean-Jacques Dessalines declares independence at Gonaives, founding Haiti as the world's first Black republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1804-independence-proclaimed, claim TL:HTI:event:1804:independence-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Christophe crowned King Henry I
claims.summary: Henry Christophe proclaims a kingdom in northern Haiti and builds the Citadelle Laferriere; the south remains a republic under Petion.

sources.label: National History Park - Citadel, Sans Souci, Ramiers

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1811-christophe-crowned-king-henry-i, claim TL:HTI:event:1811:christophe-crowned-king-henry-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The French indemnity
claims.summary: France recognises Haitian independence only in exchange for an indemnity of 150 million francs, burdening Haiti with crippling debt.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1825-the-french-indemnity, claim TL:HTI:event:1825:the-french-indemnity, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Boyer unifies Hispaniola
claims.summary: After Santo Domingo declares independence, Haitian forces move east and govern the whole island — a republic of former slaves administering the oldest European colony in the Americas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1821-boyer-unifies-hispaniola, claim TL:HTI:event:1821:boyer-unifies-hispaniola, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dominican Republic secedes
claims.summary: The eastern, Spanish-speaking part of Hispaniola breaks from Haitian rule to form the independent Dominican Republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1844-dominican-republic-secedes, claim TL:HTI:event:1844:dominican-republic-secedes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Second Empire of Faustin Soulouque
claims.summary: General Soulouque makes himself emperor and spends his reign in repeated attempts to reconquer the east.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1849-the-second-empire-of-faustin-soulouque, claim TL:HTI:event:1849:the-second-empire-of-faustin-soulouque, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The United States recognises Haiti
claims.summary: Fifty-eight years after independence — and only in the middle of its own civil war — Washington recognises the republic a slave revolt had founded.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Haiti
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1862-the-united-states-recognises-haiti, claim TL:HTI:event:1862:the-united-states-recognises-haiti, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: United States occupation
claims.summary: U.S. Marines occupy Haiti for nineteen years, controlling its finances and building infrastructure amid widespread resentment and resistance.

sources.label: U.S. Invasion and Occupation of Haiti, 1915-34
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1915-united-states-occupation, claim TL:HTI:event:1915:united-states-occupation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Papa Doc Duvalier takes power
claims.summary: Francois Duvalier becomes president and establishes a personal dictatorship enforced by the Tontons Macoutes, declaring himself president for life.

sources.label: Haiti: Military regimes and the Duvaliers

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1957-papa-doc-duvalier-takes-power, claim TL:HTI:event:1957:papa-doc-duvalier-takes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: President for Life
claims.summary: Duvalier proclaims himself president for life and crushes an uprising at Jeremie with hundreds killed; his anti-communism keeps American support flowing.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1964-president-for-life, claim TL:HTI:event:1964:president-for-life, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Baby Doc
claims.summary: A popular uprising drives Jean-Claude 'Baby Doc' Duvalier into exile, ending a 29-year family dictatorship in which an estimated 40,000-60,000 Haitians were killed.

sources.label: Haiti: Military regimes and the Duvaliers

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1986-fall-of-baby-doc, claim TL:HTI:event:1986:fall-of-baby-doc, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Aristide elected
claims.summary: Jean-Bertrand Aristide wins Haiti's first free presidential election; he is overthrown in 1991 and restored in 1994.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1990-aristide-elected, claim TL:HTI:event:1990:aristide-elected, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Twenty thousand US troops restore Aristide
claims.summary: An American-led intervention reverses the 1991 coup and returns the elected president to office.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-1994-twenty-thousand-us-troops-restore-aristide, claim TL:HTI:event:1994:twenty-thousand-us-troops-restore-aristide, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Aristide leaves again; the UN deploys
claims.summary: An armed rebellion drives Aristide from the country a second time; US Marines land and a UN stabilisation force takes over, staying until 2019.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-2004-aristide-leaves-again-the-un-deploys, claim TL:HTI:event:2004:aristide-leaves-again-the-un-deploys, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Catastrophic earthquake
claims.summary: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake devastates Port-au-Prince; death-toll estimates vary widely and remain disputed, with around three million people affected.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-2010-catastrophic-earthquake, claim TL:HTI:event:2010:catastrophic-earthquake, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hurricane Matthew
claims.summary: The strongest storm to strike the region in a decade kills hundreds and destroys thousands of homes.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-2016-hurricane-matthew, claim TL:HTI:event:2016:hurricane-matthew, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of President Moise
claims.summary: President Jovenel Moise is assassinated at his home, accelerating Haiti's slide into gang rule and state collapse.

sources.label: UN Security Council approves new force for Haiti amid gang violence

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-2021-assassination-of-president-moise, claim TL:HTI:event:2021:assassination-of-president-moise, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A second great earthquake
claims.summary: Five weeks after the assassination, a magnitude 7.2 quake in the south-west kills some 2,200 people.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Haiti: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and the slave colony of Saint-Domingue to the world's first Black republic.", terralore.co/country/HTI/chronicle#ev-2021-a-second-great-earthquake, claim TL:HTI:event:2021:a-second-great-earthquake, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Transitional council and security mission
claims.summary: A transitional presidential council and a Kenyan-led security mission seek to restore order as gangs control most of the capital and a strengthened UN-authorised force is approved.

sources.label: UN Security Council approves new force for Haiti amid gang violence
